Let me break this down step by step. First, I usually make it a habit to get coffee for my co-worker every morning. It's something I do without being asked, just to be helpful. But this morning, I didn't do it because I knew they were out of town. So, I need to assess if this action was appropriate or not. I think about why I started picking up coffee for them in the first place. It was probably to be kind and supportive, maybe to make their mornings a bit easier. It's a small gesture, but it shows that I care about their well-being. So, not doing it when they're not there might seem like a change in my behavior. But wait, they were out of town, so they wouldn't be in the office. That means they wouldn't need the coffee anyway. It's not like I stopped doing it just because I felt like it; it was because the situation changed. So, in this case, not picking up the coffee was a practical decision based on their absence. I also consider if there's any negative implication of not getting the coffee. Since they're not there, there's no one to receive it, so it doesn't affect them. It's not like I'm neglecting them or being rude. It's just a situation where the action wasn't necessary. Another angle is whether my co-worker would expect me to get coffee even when they're not around. I don't think so because they wouldn't be there to drink it. So, it makes sense that I didn't do it this time. I also think about the effort involved. Picking up coffee every morning takes time and effort. If they're not there, it's a waste of both. So, it's more efficient to skip it when they're away. In terms of workplace dynamics, being considerate is important. But in this case, my action was still considerate because I was thinking about their needs and adjusting my behavior accordingly. It shows that I'm paying attention and not just going through the motions without thinking. I also wonder if there's any potential misunderstanding. Maybe someone else might think I stopped because I'm upset or something, but I don't think that's the case here. It's a clear situation where the absence made the action unnecessary. So, putting it all together, I think it's right not to pick up the coffee because my co-worker wasn't there. It was a practical and considerate decision based on the circumstances.
